text.p: BLANTYRE, March 4 (Reuter) These are the leading stories in the Malawi Press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Members of parliament for Alliance for Democracy (AFORD) are today meeting in Mzuzu, northern Malawi, in a crucial meeting to decide whether to return to parliament or not and break the stalemate of parliamentary boycott by the opposition.
- A 30-year-old man was stabbed to death at a party on Sunday in an orgy of violence that led angry friends of the deceased to burn down the killers home, eyewitnesses said on Monday.

- Main opposition Malawi Congress Party (MCP) vice president Gwanda Chakuamba and Alliance for Democracy (AFORD) president Chakufwa Chihana met for the second time with President Bakili Muluzi over the weekend to try and resolve the opposition's parliamentary boycott issue.

- Irate United Democratic Front (UDF) supporters on Monday set ablaze a house after dousing it with petrol in Ndirande township in Blantyre after a man was stabbed to death during a fight over a girl on Sunday.

- The Law Society of Malawi over the weekend replaced its executive committee following allegations that the society had dismissed as untrue reports that it was pushing for a commission of inquiry to investigate Chief Justice Richard Banda for reportedly influencing a High Court judge to rule in favour of government.
